newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian money market rate soars to 11.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian money market rate soars to 11.3 pct.

text.p: Croatia's average money market rate soared to 11.3 pct from 9.8 pct on Monday as some creditors raised their interest rates amid growing demand and lack of fresh kuna supply, dealers said.
They said deals were made for the entire offer of 33.6 million kuna on the Zagreb money market, and borrowers' demand for another 20 million kuna could not be met.
Fresh loans accounted for 20.8 million kuna of the daily trade.
The highest rate of 17 percent was struck for a smaller one-month loan.
The overall call money rate edged up 10 basis points to 9.6 percent and dealers said some call money borrowings were made at a higher rate of 10 percent.
Overnight trade at the weekend totalled 46 million kuna, which ten banks used to square their positions and another one to maintain its mandatory reserve. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
